reviews.title: All our sensitive info hacked and stolen
reviews.text:
Lack of communication is frustrating.

They need to say which data was taken, what was encrypted or readable, whether the encryption held up, and which users are affected—then explain what each group needs to do. “Change everything” without proper explanation?

reviews.title: Please DO NOT buy or use this.
reviews.text: Been using mSecure since 2011 without any issues until last week when I got the vague email saying they had basically been hacked and our passwords are compromised. Supposedly, this was impossible from what was said previously by the developer! Since the initial email the company has gone completely dark and what for a better term ditched their customers and left them to get on with it! No further updates or announcements made. It wouldn’t surprise me if they wait for the dust to settle and carry on as if nothing happened, or more likely rebrand and carry on. If you still choose to use or even buy the program, you’re leaving yourself and the data you share with them exposed for who knows to see and use. How can mSecure ever be trusted again.

reviews.title: This is a Shady Company
reviews.text:
As many of the reviews have noted, this company recently had a data breach. I’ve been trying to cancel my account subscription with them for the past week and they are refusing to acknowledge my request.

I’ve sent several emails, and I only received one generic response about how deleting my account will not resolve the fact that my data may have already been exposed. They basically replied that they’re going to continue charging me whether I like it or not.

Unfortunately, my account was set up years ago with my subscription charged through some international website that they use — not through Apple. If they don’t cancel my subscription within a few days, I’ll have to take care of it through my credit card company.

It has been surprisingly frustrating dealing with this company. I never expected such unethical business practices.

reviews.title: Avoid. Hacked
reviews.text:
Was a good product right up to the point where they got hacked and showed that they have no clue how to handle a security breach.  Users - both current AND past - were emailed and told mseven had identified a security breach and they advised users to change every security credential they stored in the mSecure password manager. No details on the specifics of the breach - just change everything folks, coz we pretty much haven’t a clue what the hackers might have got. Oh - and by the way, we kept details of PREVIOUS users who don’t even use the product any longer. So if you ever used mSecure and you haven’t changed your passwords since, you’re pretty stuffed too. 

Shockingly awful service. Very poor communication with users, and deeply questionable ‘zero knowledge architecture’.

reviews.title: Pathetically, poor handling of security breach
reviews.text:
I’ve been a paying mSecure customer for years, trusting this company to protect some of my most sensitive personal and financial information.

Receiving a vague email about a security breach, without clearly explaining what was compromised, which customers were affected, or whether my passwords are at risk, is completely unacceptable.

Customers should not have to investigate a security incident themselves to determine whether they need to change hundreds of passwords. I use Wi-Fi synchronization exclusively, yet the company provided no clear explanation of whether customers like me were affected.

For a company whose entire business is built around password security and customer trust, this lack of transparency is deeply disappointing.

Security breaches can happen. It’s how a company responds that defines its integrity. mSecure needs to do much better. My confidence in this company has been seriously shaken.

They didn't say what happened, what was accessed, or whether our vaults were exposed. A password manager's entire job is trust, and leaving long-time customers to guess is absurd. They don't deserve anyone's business.

reviews.title: Hacked (Nov 2026) App - DO NOT BUY
reviews.text:
Tl;dr: DO NOT BUY! THIS APP WILL GET HACKED AND THEN THE DEVS OR THEIR 3RD PARTIES WILL TELL YOU TO JUST GO IMMEDIATELY CHANGE EVERYTHING AND LITTLE MORE THAN AN OBLIGATORY “SORRRRY.” THERE ARE MUCH BETTER OPTIONS/PRODUCTS NOW, CHOOSE THEM LIKE I DID TODAY (manually changing a thousand records and migrating my accounts to a safer, more secure product as we speak). 

Full Story: Wow. So I have been with this guy and his app since the VERY beginning (over 10 years). Guy took my money, provided me a false sense of security, got lucky he was so small he wasn’t targeted, and now like all the other bad devs/apps/companies/governments he slacked off on his security layering, zero trust model, and made stupid errors so now everyone who ever used this app (or still does) just got notified they were hacked!!! 

No deep details, no offers to help or refund people, just an empty “whoopsie” notice like all the other awful mopes out there letting these hacks occur and then being like “hey, not my fault, it happens.”But I am a senior infosec SME people: tech security is my job. The more I learn about what happened and see how this guy and his hired 3rd party are handling this breach (barely any info, no real support just blackhole tickets served by 3rd party that likely is why this fool got us all jacked, etc.) the more I realize I NEVER SHOULD HAVE TRUSTED MSEVEN “SECURITY”!SOFTWARE.

Perhaps if this developer spent more time on what matters (security) and less time developing a banner that nags paying customers that they should pay even more for an upgrade, this would not have happened.

reviews.title: Security incident
reviews.text:
I've been a paying mSecure user for years, but the way they've handled the recent security incident is unacceptable.
 
On November 2–3, 2026, they emailed users about "suspicious activity" and told us to "immediately secure all confidential information" — change passwords, reset 2FA, remove passkeys. That's it. They did not say what was accessed, how the breach happened, or whether our encrypted vaults or master passwords were compromised. For a password manager, that omission is the whole ballgame.
 
Worse, the advice contradicts their own marketing. mSecure advertises a "zero-knowledge" model where only the user can decrypt data. If that were true, a server breach shouldn't require me to change every password stored in the app. So either the encryption isn't what they claim, or the breach was serious enough to compromise keys — and they won't tell us which.
 
The notice itself was so vague that many users assumed it was phishing. That's a failure of communication on its own.
 
I'm now facing hours of work changing passwords across dozens of accounts because mSecure won't tell me what actually happened. That's not acceptable from any company, least of all one entrusted with every credential I own.
 
Until mSeven Software publishes a clear, detailed incident report, I can't recommend this app to anyone.

The new device was bult from the old one, so the configuration matched. By trying to establish a connection, I erroneously deleted my account on the new phone. This immediately impacted all access, even on my desktop. I have a local backup file. And I created a ticket through mSecure support. It has now been 4 days. I received 1 message, which told me how to backup my file from on offline device. But nothing on how to reestablish my account!  I now have to evaluate moving to a new product, just to get back up and running!  I am disappointed in mSecure service when I need it the most!

reviews.title: An app that forgets you already paid for it
reviews.text:
Never as good as the old version but generally ok. The app seems to be on the downhill slide now though. It's doing the "move things behind the subscription paywall" part of the spiral. 
They seem to forget many of us already paid for the app and have no interest in cloud services or subscriptions.

But a password manager MUST be reliable and also have an export feature that doesn’t require an hour of massaging to be usable. Completely unacceptable. reviews.title: They Keep Winning Arguments I Never Made
reviews.text:
I've used mSecure since 2010. I paid in 2010 and I paid again in 2016. For years I was a loyal customer who recommended it freely. I'm the exact person this developer claims to protect, and I'm the one writing this.

Then the deal changed under me. The product I'd already bought twice got reorganized into something I didn't recognize and routed into a subscription that rose every year. That's my complaint. Hold onto it, because the developer won't.

Their first reply implied I'd said things that "aren't true." Their latest one spends several hundred words defending the phrase "Universal App" and denying "semantic tricks." But I never built my complaint on "Universal App." That's their word, and they picked it because it's the one battle they can win. Writing paragraphs about it while skipping the actual grievance isn't an answer. It's misdirection, and now they've done it twice in writing.

Look at their own defense. They call the shift to paid upgrades and subscriptions "a common, software industry standard." That isn't a denial. It's an admission with better posture. "Everyone does it" concedes exactly what I said happened. The 66% discount and the free Essentials tier aren't proof of innocence. They're the severance check for a contract the company rewrote on its own.

reviews.title: I Liked mSecure4 Much Better 😔
reviews.text: Some years back I purchased mSecure5 but didn’t ever used it much because I liked 4 better. Recently 4 wouldn’t open up any more, so luckily I was able to open up 5 & import all my data from 4. I just upgraded to premium but the interface looks exactly the same as 5 “Essentials” + they charge you yearly just to have it. Premium isn’t a “once-$-done” type of purchase. It’s supposed to have “an improved Ui, but it looks exactly the same. It’s supposed to have other extra features too but I haven’t discovered what they are. Also, when you create a new template for something with things in a certain order & you go to use that template the categories are not all there, & those that are are not in the order you put them in. I am not liking mSecure 5 so far & may have to ditch them for another password keeper soon. How frustrating & dissappointing. 😖
